author: CC
prose: THE HEARTBEAT DIES WITH THE TERMINAL WINDOW, and it just did. superclaude spawns the ground loop at launchers/superclaude:229 with `setsid`, and setsid leaves the controlling tty but NOT the cgroup — measured today: a setsid'd child of this session reported the identical cgroup path as its parent. The spawn also happens BEFORE the exec into the memory scope at :292, so the loop inherits whatever cgroup launched superclaude, which in practice is the Konsole scope. On 2026-08-18 the kernel oom-killed the claude binary at 14:57:31, systemd marked app-org.kde.konsole-b1d62b21cfc74a57b8e15d874590bdc6.scope 'Failed with result oom-kill' at 14:57:43, and the heartbeat went with it: its own trail at ~/.cairn/logs/ground_loop/0/diagnostics.jsonl carries exactly three loop starts today — 14:52:55, then 14:58:01, then 15:33:34 — with nothing between the kill and the restart. Yesterday's cgroup patch (cairn 124442b) made the SESSION die alone; the two things the session is supposed to outlive, the heartbeat and the sudo relay, still die with the window that started it. The fix is the shape I used by hand to restart it: parent the loop on the user manager rather than on the caller — `systemd-run --user --unit=cairn-ground-loop` puts it at /user.slice/user-1000.slice/user@1000.service/app.slice/cairn-ground-loop.service, a sibling of both Konsole and the session scope, and it survives either one dying. Akien's own ruling stands untouched by this: 'THE INTENTION IS THE GROUND LOOP IS ALWAYS UP. IF ITS NOT UP, LAUNCHING AN ENTRY POINT LAUNCHES IT. NO SYSTEM LEVEL STARTUP REQUIRED.' A transient unit is still no system-level startup — nothing is installed, nothing survives a reboot, an entry point still starts it.
